$comment: Repositories the sweep clones, pinned by SHA. Every entry carries a licence, because `--promote` refuses to excerpt copyleft into an MIT project and the field is what makes that policy enforceable rather than aspirational.

repos.why: The best single all-round pin: real UI copy and locale bundles, AND dense localStorage keys, enums and persisted values. It exercises recall and precision in one clone, which no single-purpose repository does.
Google's own reference app: real `<plurals>` in `res/values*/strings.xml` and Compose `pluralStringResource`. The only Android pin permissive AND idiomatic enough to trust.
gettext, densely: `.po`/`.pot` fixtures with `msgid_plural` and `msgstr[n]`, plus `ngettext` in source. Small enough to clone nightly.
Fluent in a shipping product rather than a toy — `l10n/*/viewer.ftl` with real selectors.
The canonical ICU source of truth: `defineMessages`, `selectordinal`, `offset:`, `select` nested inside `plural`.

The CONTROL. A tiny repository with no i18n at all, where the oracle should find essentially nothing. A pile of confirmed misses here means the locators are too broad — a pure precision signal with no recall confound, for the cost of one small clone.
Thousands of `.po` files plus `blocktrans` template tags. Scoped, or the clone dominates the run.
Apple `.strings` and `.stringsdict` under a permissive licence, which is rare. Verify the stringsdict locator actually fires at pin time; the sweep report says whether it did.
Monorepo shape, to exercise per-package coverage. The realistic failure in the wild is not a missed line but a missed PACKAGE, and a repo-wide percentage hides that completely.

$qt: Qt is deliberately NOT pinned. Every substantial, representative Qt codebase is GPL or LGPL; reading one to measure is fine, but pinning copyleft in an MIT project's benchmark manifest — in a report that quotes lines — is a mess nobody needs. Qt is covered offline in bench/corpus/plural-unread-dialects, where the interesting behaviour (the TypeScript grammar choking on XML) is fully reproducible anyway.
